title: Science: Everyday Materials 🧱
summary:
1. Where do materials come from?
• Naturally: They come from nature! Examples: Wood and cotton (from plants), wool (from animals), rock and metal (from the ground).
• Manufactured: Made by humans! Examples: Plastic, paper (made from wood), and glass (made from sand).

2. Properties of Materials
A property describes what a material is like.
• Strong (hard to break), flexible (bends easily), light (not heavy), smooth, waterproof (keeps water out).
• See-through (like glass) or not see-through (like wood).

3. Testing & Choosing
We test materials to see their properties. Then we can put the results in a block graph. We must choose the right material for the job!

4. Changing Materials
Some materials change into completely new things! If we burn wood, it turns into ash. If metal gets wet, it can rust.
